Marissa / Olivia —

Quick security lens on the inventory: a few things stand out that we should treat as gating for evidence and rollout.

1) Module signing: any shared Terraform modules that are referenced by both prod and staging must be artifact-signed (or pinned with immutable checksum) — we need either signed releases or a verification step in CI.
2) Secret handling: I see several Helm charts using plain-file values templates. Replace those with sealed secrets or reference to KMS-backed secrets in the runbook.
3) Egress & svc accounts: We need a mapping of service accounts to minimum egress ACLs. For SOC2 proof, provide an annotated policy per account and a sample audit log demonstrating policy enforcement.

Minimal evidence bundle (what Redwood can accept):
- module-release manifest (tag + checksum)
- CI build logs showing artifact promotion
- a signed commit or a release pipeline step (we can accept YAML from your CI showing signing step)
- a sample FW rule + audit entry (1 day window)

I'll attach a short checklist I use for these reviews. If Acme can provide the first two items ahead of the tech review, we'll be able to spin a preliminary evidence package quickly.

Regards,
Kimberly
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Team —

I ran a quick pass on the spreadsheet and sketched an approach in a small note (attached) and opened a PR on the sample repo where we can stage the pruning changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/acme-priv-iac/pull/42

Highlights / suggestions:
- Split shared modules into two tracks: 
  a) "Core" (networking, auth, ingress) — require module signing + non-breaking compatibility shim.
  b) "App" (metrics, sidecar configs) — allow aggressive pruning with integration tests gated in a dedicated feature pipeline.
- CI changes: add a promotion job that publishes a signed artifact and a lightweight integration test job that runs in a sandbox VPC (can be ephemeral). This keeps staging green while allowing pruning.
- Helm charts: convert values files that contain secrets into templates referencing a secrets provider; add a Helm test that asserts no plain-text secrets exist.

Attachment: gitops-pruning-plan.md (markdown, 6KB)

I'll be ready to walk through the PR on Tuesday. Jordan — can you outline the gating jobs you'd want on the GitHub Actions / Jenkins side?

-Karthik
